children: Policy support is unlikely to be the major driver of a consumption recovery in China, says Daniel Zhang, former Alibaba Group chairman. Consumer demand in China has been in a prolonged slumped, prompting a nationwide campaign to boost spending through vouchers and subsidies. Speaking at the FutureChina Global Forum in Singapore, Zhang, who is now managing partner at FirstLight Capital, said real change usually happens when consumers spontaneously embrace new spending habits, describing a sort of ripple effect of consumption: "If a girl goes to a salon to get her hair done today, the salon worker makes some money and goes to get her nails done tomorrow. Then the nail technician has extra money to buy clothes online." (tracy.qu@wsj.com)
